title: Repo skeleton
acceptance: docker compose up starts Postgres, the Go API and the mock provider
make verify passes
Every later slice has a fixed place for its spec, plan, decisions and progress

title: Trim the Vue template into frontend/
acceptance: FR-1: pnpm dev starts the app with no console errors
FR-2: / redirects to /campaigns/new
FR-3: /campaigns/new, /campaigns and /campaigns/123 show a placeholder page in the default layout
FR-4: an unknown route shows the 404 page
FR-5: the sidebar shows Campaign Composer and two links, with no team switcher and no user menu
FR-6: the header shows the sidebar toggle, the page search and the light and dark toggle only
FR-7: the light and dark choice stays after a reload
FR-8: the page search lists only the sidebar pages
NFR-1: pnpm build passes with no type errors
NFR-2: pnpm lint passes
NFR-3: pnpm test:run passes. Tests for removed code are deleted. Tests for kept code are not deleted
NFR-4: no file in frontend/src imports a removed file or package
NFR-5: no text refers to the template demo data
NFR-6: package.json name, version and private are set, with no template metadata or hook tools
NFR-7: pnpm-lock.yaml is generated again
NFR-8: frontend/LICENSE keeps the MIT notice
NFR-9: src/types/*.d.ts are generated again and refer to no removed file
NFR-10: .env.example has only the three VITE_SERVER_API values

title: Seed users
acceptance: FR-1: seed applies all goose migrations before it inserts data.
FR-2: On an empty database, seed inserts SEED_USERS random users plus the edge-case users from goal.md.
FR-3: If users contains rows, seed makes no change and exits with code 0.
FR-4: With SEED_RESET=true, seed deletes all users and events, then inserts them again.
FR-5: The same SEED_RANDOM and seed time give the same rows.
FR-6: Each language is tr or en. Each country is TR or US. Check constraints reject other values. Each TR user is tr and each US user is en.
FR-7: Each email is unique and ends with @example.com.
FR-8: Each phone matches ^\+905\d{9}$ for TR or ^\+1\d{3}55501\d{2}$ for US.
FR-9: Each city is in the list for the user's country.
FR-10: The country, language and consent ratios are within 3 percentage points of the table in goal.md.
FR-11: For each user, the summary columns are equal to the values calculated from events.
FR-12: Each purchase event has an amount greater than 0. Each cart_add event has a null amount.
FR-13: The example brief's rule from goal.md, with language = tr, selects at least 1 user.
NFR-1: seed inserts 5,000 users in less than 10 seconds. Use pgx CopyFrom.
NFR-2: The migrations add indexes on users.city, users.language, users.last_cart_add_at, users.last_purchase_at and events.user_id.
NFR-3: docker-compose.yml has a seed service with restart: "no". api depends on it with condition: service_completed_successfully.
NFR-4: make up starts the stack on an empty volume. The users table then contains the seeded rows.
NFR-5: The generator is a pure function of the random seed and the seed time. Tests run it with no database.

NFR-6: Tests for FR-1 to FR-4 and FR-11 run against Postgres. They read TEST_DATABASE_URL. make test starts a temporary Postgres container and sets this variable. Without the variable, go test skips these tests.
NFR-7: make verify passes.
NFR-8: The seed binary imports nothing from internal/ except config, store and seed.

title: Mock SMS and email provider
acceptance: FR-1. POST /v1/sms and POST /v1/email with a valid body return 202 with a new id. The provider stores the message.

FR-2. A request that is not valid returns 400 with code: invalid_request. The provider stores nothing. This includes an SMS body over 160 characters, a subject over 80 characters, a bad to and a missing required field.
FR-3. The provider counts characters as runes. An SMS body of 160 Turkish characters, for example ş, gets 202. A body of 161 characters gets 400.
FR-4. A repeat request with the same body and reference gets 202 and a new id. The provider stores both. duplicate_deliveries goes up by 1.
FR-5. When a channel is over its rate limit, the provider returns 429 with a Retry-After header of 1 or more. A 429 on sms does not use an email token.
FR-6. With MOCK_RATE_PER_SEC=100 and the default burst, 200 requests sent at once to one channel get at least one 429. 100 requests sent at a steady 100 per second get no 429.
FR-7. X-Mock-Fail: 500 and X-Mock-Fail: 503 return that status. The provider stores nothing.
FR-8. X-Mock-Fail: slow returns 202 after MOCK_SLOW_DELAY. The provider stores the message.
FR-9. X-Mock-Fail: lost closes the connection with no response. The provider stores the message. The client gets a transport error, not an HTTP status.
FR-10. X-Mock-Fail: 429 returns 429 with Retry-After: 1 and uses no token. X-Mock-Fail: none gets no random failure. Any other value gets 400.
FR-11. With all three rates at 0, 1,000 valid requests get 202.
FR-12. With a fixed MOCK_RANDOM, the count of each failure mode over 10,000 requests is within 1 percentage point of its rate.
FR-13. GET /v1/messages filters by channel, to and reference. It sorts newest first and applies limit and offset. total counts all matches.
FR-14. GET /v1/stats gives each counter from goal.md for each channel. The counters match the responses that the provider sent.
FR-15. DELETE /v1/messages returns 204. After it, GET /v1/messages gives total: 0 and all counters are 0.
FR-16. An env var that is not valid stops the process at startup with a clear error. This includes a rate outside 0 to 1, a sum of rates over 1, and a bad duration.
NFR-1. The handlers are safe for concurrent requests. A test sends 500 requests from 50 goroutines. delivered is then equal to the count of 202 responses plus lost responses.
NFR-2. Tests use httptest and an injected clock and sleep function. No test waits for MOCK_SLOW_DELAY or for the rate limiter in real time.
NFR-3. Tests set the failure rates and do not depend on the defaults.
NFR-4. docker-compose.yml passes each MOCK_* env var to mock-provider, with the defaults from goal.md. .env.example lists them as comments.
NFR-5. make up starts mock-provider. curl -X POST localhost:8081/v1/sms with a valid body and X-Mock-Fail: none returns 202.
NFR-6. cmd/mockprovider imports nothing from internal/ except config and mockprovider. internal/mockprovider imports nothing from internal/.
NFR-7. make verify passes.

title: Segment rules
acceptance: FR-1. POST /api/segments/preview with the example brief and the default mock returns 200. The response has the rule, the description and an audience with email and sms of 1 or more.
FR-2. Sanitization removes control characters except \n and \t, format characters and <brief> tags, with case ignored. It normalizes to NFC and trims the text. A table test covers each step.

FR-3. A brief with no letter, or with more than 1,000 runes after sanitization, returns 400 with code: invalid_brief. The LLM client gets no call. A brief of 1,000 Turkish runes, for example ş, is valid.
FR-4. A body over 16 KiB, a body that is not valid JSON, or a body with no brief returns 400 with code: invalid_request.

FR-5. The validator rejects each case in "Validation". A table test has one or more cases for each item. The cases include an unknown field, an unknown operator, a wrong operator for a field, a string "30" for within_days, a city not on the list, between with low over high, an in list of 21 values, depth 4, 21 conditions, an unknown key and data after the object.
FR-6. The validator returns all errors with a path, not only the first.
FR-7. SQL injection in a value fails validation. Examples: "Istanbul' OR 1=1 --" for city, and "city; DROP TABLE users" as a field name.
FR-8. For each field and operator, the compiler gives the expected SQL text and parameters. No value from the rule is in the SQL text.
FR-9. With a fixed clock, within_days, older_than_days and age give the expected time and date parameters.
FR-10. An empty root group compiles to TRUE and counts all users. An empty nested group fails validation.

FR-11. If the first LLM answer fails validation and the second is valid, the response is 200. The second request to the mock contains the first answer as a tool call. It also contains the validation errors as a tool result with the error flag.
FR-12. If both LLM answers fail validation, the response is 422 with code: segment_invalid and the errors in details. The backend runs no count query.
FR-13. An unsupported answer returns 422 with code: segment_unsupported and the reason. The backend runs no count query.
FR-14. An ok answer with unmapped returns 200 with the unmapped list. More than 5 items, or an item over 200 runes, fails validation.

FR-15. Against Postgres, the audience counts are equal to the counts that a test calculates in Go from the seeded users. The test covers the example rule, an or group, an age between rule and an empty root.

FR-16. audience.languages has one entry for each language in the audience, sorted by reachable from high to low, then by code. A language with reachable of 0 is not in the list. A rule with country in [TR, US] gives two entries. The example rule gives only tr.
FR-17. A rule that selects no users returns 200 with all counts at 0 and an empty languages list.
FR-18. The same rule always gives the same description. Each field and each operator has a test.

FR-19. An LLM client error returns 502 with code: llm_error. A timeout returns 504 with code: llm_timeout. A refusal returns 502 with code: llm_refused and no repair round. The test uses the mock and an injected timeout, with no real wait.
FR-20. The system prompt contains each allowlist field, each operator and each city. A test builds the prompt and checks this.
FR-21. The user message puts the sanitized brief between <brief> and </brief>. The system prompt does not contain the brief.

FR-22. On /campaigns/new, the operator enters a brief and clicks "Find audience". The page shows "Generating segment…" while the request runs, then the description, the counts, the languages and the unmapped notes.
FR-23. On an API error, the page shows the API message and keeps the brief. The page shows unmapped and reason as text, not as HTML.

FR-24. For each user in the result of the recipients function for sms, sms_consent is true. The same is true for email. The test uses a rule that matches the seed users with no consent, and they are not in either result.
FR-25. no_consent is equal to matched minus reachable, in the top level and in each language entry.
FR-26. A first answer with no submit_segment call gets a repair round. The repair request ends with a user text message, not a tool result.
NFR-1. The compiler accepts only the validated rule type. No function in internal/segment takes raw JSON and returns SQL.

NFR-2. The allowlist is in one table. The validator, the compiler, the description, the prompt and the tool schema read it. A test adds a fake field to a copy of the table and checks that all five use it.
NFR-3. The count query has a 2 second statement timeout. A timeout returns 503 with code: db_unavailable.
NFR-4. Tests use the mock LLM. No test reads ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. With LLM_MODE=mock, the api starts with no key.
NFR-5. Logs contain no brief text and no API key.
NFR-6. internal/segment imports nothing from internal/. internal/llm imports nothing from internal/ except config.
NFR-7. The Postgres tests read TEST_DATABASE_URL, as in slice 02. Without it, go test skips them.
NFR-8. Frontend tests mock the API. pnpm test:run, pnpm build and CI=true pnpm lint pass.
NFR-9. make up with no .env starts the stack. The example brief on /campaigns/new shows an audience.
NFR-10. make verify passes.
NFR-11. The recipients function is the only function in internal/segment that returns user rows. Its channel argument is a type with two values. No argument turns off the consent condition.

title: Content generation
acceptance: FR-1. POST /api/content/generate with the example brief, the example rule and the default mock returns 200 with text/event-stream. The events are audience, then one or more draft events and one final event for tr, then done.
FR-2. These bodies return 400 with code: invalid_request: a body over 16 KiB, a body that is not valid JSON, and a body with no brief or no rule. The LLM client gets no call.
FR-3. A brief that fails the slice 04 checks returns 400 with code: invalid_brief. The LLM client gets no call.

FR-4. A rule that fails the slice 04 validator returns 400 with code: invalid_rule and the errors in details. The cases include an unknown field and "Istanbul' OR 1=1 --" for city. The backend runs no query.
FR-5. A rule with no reachable user returns 422 with code: empty_audience. The LLM client gets no call.
FR-6. The backend makes one LLM call for each language in the audience. A rule with country in [TR, US] gives calls for tr and en. Each request names its language in the user message.
FR-7. The variable parser accepts zero, one or more {{first_name}}. It rejects {{last_name}}, {{ first_name }}, {{first_name}, a single {{ and a single }}. A table test covers each case.
FR-8. The renderer replaces each {{first_name}} with the given name. Text with no variable stays the same. It does no HTML escaping.

FR-9. The validator counts runes after rendering with the longest first name. The test uses a longest name of 20 runes. An SMS of 154 runes with one {{first_name}} (14 runes) renders to 160 runes and passes. An SMS of 155 runes with one variable renders to 161 and fails. The subject passes at 80 rendered runes and fails at 81. Turkish characters, for example ş, count as 1.

FR-10. The validator rejects each case in "Validation". A table test has one or more cases for each row. The cases include these: an unknown key, a missing field, and an empty field after trim a \n in the subject, and a control character an HTML tag in each field, and data after the object It returns all errors with a path.
FR-11. A limit error gives the rendered length and the limit.

FR-12. The audience query gives the longest first name for each language. It counts only users with consent on one or more channels. A Postgres test compares it with a value that the test calculates in Go from the seed users.

FR-13. If the first answer fails validation and the second passes, the stream has draft, retry, draft and final for that language. The second mock request contains the first answer as a tool call and the errors as a tool result with the error flag.
FR-14. If both answers fail, the language gets an error event with code: content_invalid and the errors in details.
FR-15. A first answer with no submit_content call gets a repair round. The repair request ends with a user text message, not a tool result.
FR-16. An answer with stop_reason: max_tokens counts as a validation failure and gets a repair round. If its tool input is not a valid JSON object, the replayed assistant turn has {} as the input.

FR-17. An LLM client error gives an error event with code: llm_error. A timeout gives code: llm_timeout. A refusal gives code: llm_refused and no repair round. The test uses the mock and an injected timeout, with no real wait.
FR-18. With two languages, an error in one language does not stop the other. The stream has a final event for the other language, then done.

FR-19. The partial JSON parser gives the correct partial content for each prefix of a valid answer. The test cuts the answer at each byte, including inside a \u escape and inside a multi-byte rune. The parser never returns an error or a field that is longer than the final field.
FR-20. The backend sends at most one draft event per 100 ms for each language, with an injected clock. The last draft before final has the full text.
FR-21. A client disconnect cancels the LLM calls of the request. The test checks that the mock sees a cancelled context.
FR-22. The system prompt contains the SMS limit, the subject limit, the variable rule and the plain text rule. It does not contain the brief. It is the same for each language and each request.
FR-23. The user message contains the language, the rule description, the longest first name length and the sanitized brief between <brief> and </brief>.
FR-24. The default mock content for tr and en passes validation with a longest first name of 30 runes.
FR-25. On /campaigns/new, a segment result with one or more languages starts content generation with no second click. The page shows "Generating content…" while the request runs.

FR-26. The page shows one card for each language. The draft text shows as a draft. On final, the card shows the final text and a counter for SMS and subject. On retry, the card shows "Fixing content…". On error, the card shows the message, and the other cards stay.
FR-27. "Regenerate content" sends the same brief and rule again. A new "Find audience" click aborts the open content request and clears the cards.
FR-28. The page shows the content as text, not as HTML. A test with x in a draft event shows the tags as text.
FR-29. An error before the stream opens shows its message in the content area. The segment result stays.
FR-30. A fallback block in the stream gives a retry event with no errors. The backend uses only the submit_content call after it. The language still has its one repair round.
NFR-1. Tests use the mock LLM. No test reads ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. With LLM_MODE=mock, the api starts with no key.
NFR-2. Logs contain no brief text, no content text and no API key.
NFR-3. internal/content imports nothing from internal/. internal/llm imports nothing from internal/ except config.
NFR-4. The variable parser and the renderer are exported from internal/content. Slice 07 can use them with no change.
NFR-5. No user row leaves the database in this slice. The content step uses only aggregate values from the audience query.
NFR-6. The Postgres tests read TEST_DATABASE_URL, as in slice 02. Without it, go test skips them.
NFR-7. Frontend tests mock the stream. pnpm test:run, pnpm build and CI=true pnpm lint pass.
NFR-8. make up with no .env starts the stack. The example brief on /campaigns/new shows the audience, then a tr card that fills in and becomes final.
NFR-9. The SSE response works with the api server settings. No server write timeout cuts a stream of 90 seconds.
NFR-10. make verify passes.

title: Review and approve
acceptance: FR-1. POST /api/content/generate with the example brief, the example rule and the default mock ends with a campaign event, then done. The database has one campaign with status = draft and one campaign_contents row for tr.
FR-2. The draft has the sanitized brief, the rule, the description, the final content, the counts and first_name_runes. The counts match CountAudience for the same rule.
FR-3. With two languages, one final and one failed, the draft has one content row. skipped_languages has the failed language.
FR-4. If all languages fail, the stream has no campaign event and the database has no new campaign.
FR-5. If the draft save fails, the stream has an error event with no language and code: draft_not_saved, then done.
FR-6. After a client disconnect, the backend saves no draft. The test checks that the database has no new campaign.
FR-7. A request with the campaign_id of a draft and the same brief and rule replaces the content of that draft. The database still has one campaign.
FR-8. A request with the campaign_id of an approved campaign, or with a different brief or rule, gives an error event with no language and code: campaign_conflict. The campaign does not change.
FR-9. PUT /api/campaigns/{id}/contents with valid edits returns 200. GET then returns the edits, trimmed.
FR-10. POST /api/campaigns/{id}/approve with valid content returns 200. The campaign has status = approved, approved_at set, and the content of the request.
FR-11. A second approval returns 200 and the same campaign. It changes nothing, also with a different body.
FR-12. Ten approvals of one draft at the same time give one approval. approved_at has one value. A Postgres test covers this.
FR-13. A save on an approved campaign returns 409 campaign_not_draft. A direct SQL update of the content of an approved campaign fails, or the store blocks it. A Postgres test covers the chosen way.

FR-14. These bodies return 400 invalid_request for save and approve: a body over 64 KiB, a body that is not valid JSON, and a body with no contents. An id of abc, 0 or -1 also returns 400. An unknown id returns 404 not_found.

FR-15. These contents return 422 content_invalid with the errors and their paths in details. A table test has one case for each: a missing language of the draft; a language that is not in the draft; the same language two times; an unknown key in an entry; an SMS of 161 runes after rendering with the first_name_runes of that language; a subject of 81 runes after rendering, and a subject with \n; {{last_name}} in a field, and an HTML tag in a field.
FR-16. An error path has the index, for example contents[1].sms. With two bad entries, details has the errors of both.

FR-17. Each save and each approval runs the audience query again and updates the counts and first_name_runes. A test adds a user with a longer first name between the draft and the approval. An SMS that fit before then fails.
FR-18. If a language of the draft has no reachable users at approval, the approval returns 422 content_invalid with the path contents[i].language. The campaign stays a draft.
FR-19. If a query fails or takes more than 2 seconds, save and approve return 503 db_unavailable and change nothing.
FR-20. GET /api/campaigns/{id} returns the campaign in the shape of goal.md.
FR-21. GET /api/campaigns returns the campaigns, the newest first, at most 100. The entries have no content text.

FR-22. GET /api/campaigns/{id}/sample returns up to 5 distinct first names for each language of the campaign. The first name is the longest. A Postgres test compares the result with a value that the test calculates in Go from the seed users.
FR-23. The sample result is the same for two calls.
FR-24. The sample query reads no column except first_name, language, id, the consent columns and the columns of the rule. A test checks the SQL text.
FR-25. On /campaigns/new, "Review & approve" is off while the content stream runs. It comes on after a campaign event. It stays off when the stream has no campaign event.
FR-26. "Regenerate content" sends the campaign_id of the current draft. A new "Find audience" sends no campaign_id.
FR-27. An error event with no language shows in the content area. The cards stay.
FR-28. The review window has the channel tabs "SMS" and "Email", and one language tab for each language of the draft.
FR-29. The SMS tab shows the SMS editor, the counter and the SMS preview. The Email tab shows the subject and body editors, their counters and the email preview.

FR-30. The counter renders with a name of first_name_runes runes and counts code points. A test with first_name_runes: 14 and an SMS of 146 runes plus one {{first_name}} shows 160 / 160. One more rune shows 161 / 160 in red, and "Save draft" and "Approve & send" are off.
FR-31. The counter is orange above 90% of the limit. It uses the --warning token.
FR-32. A field with {{last_name}}, an empty field or a subject with a line break shows an error line. "Save draft" and "Approve & send" are off. The language tab shows an error mark.
FR-33. The preview renders {{first_name}} with the selected sample name. The first sample is the longest name, with "(longest)" in its label. The preview shows x as text, not as HTML.
FR-34. If the sample request fails, the preview uses "Alex" and shows a note. "Approve & send" still works.
FR-35. The footer and the confirm popup name each skipped language. The confirm totals add only the languages of the draft.
FR-36. "Save draft" sends one PUT with all languages and shows "Draft saved." on success.
FR-37. "Cancel" with unsaved edits asks "Discard your changes?". With no edits, it closes at once.
FR-38. "Approve & send" opens the confirm popup. "Back" closes it and keeps the edits. "Send now" sends one approval with the edited content of all languages.
FR-39. While the approval runs, "Send now" and "Back" are off. A double click sends one request.
FR-40. On 200, the page goes to /campaigns/{id}.
FR-41. On 422 content_invalid, each error shows under its field, on the correct language tab. An error with no field shows in a banner.
FR-42. For an approved campaign, the review window shows the content read-only, with no "Save draft" and no "Approve & send".

FR-43. /campaigns lists the campaigns with the number, the description, the languages, the status badge and the time. A click on a draft opens the review window. A click on an approved campaign goes to /campaigns/{id}. With no campaigns, the page shows "No campaigns yet".

FR-44. /campaigns/{id} shows the campaign number, the status badge, the description and one read-only card for each language with its counts. A draft also shows "Review & approve". A 404 shows "Campaign not found" and a link to /campaigns.
NFR-1. Tests use the mock LLM. No test reads ANTHROPIC_API_KEY.
NFR-2. Logs contain no brief text, no content text and no API key.
NFR-3. Save and approve use content.Validate and content.Render from slice 05. The browser counter has a unit test with the same cases as FR-9 of slice 05.
NFR-4. internal/campaign imports nothing from internal/ except content, segment and store.
NFR-5. The campaign tables store no user row. Only the sample endpoint sends first names to the browser. No endpoint sends a surname, an email address or a phone number.
NFR-6. The review window and the list have no hard-coded colour. All colours come from the theme tokens. They work in the light theme and in the dark theme.
NFR-7. At 360 px width, the review window fills the screen, and /campaigns and the window have no horizontal scroll. A headless Chrome check at 360 px and at 1280 px shows this.
NFR-8. The tabs, the dialog and the confirm popups work with the keyboard. The focus stays in the open dialog.
NFR-9. The Postgres tests read TEST_DATABASE_URL, as in slice 02. Without it, go test skips them.
NFR-10. Frontend tests mock the API. pnpm test:run, pnpm build and CI=true pnpm lint pass.

NFR-11. make up with no .env starts the stack. The example brief on /campaigns/new makes a draft. The draft shows on /campaigns. A click opens the review window. "Approve & send", then "Send now", opens /campaigns/{id} with the status "Approved".
NFR-12. make verify passes.
